title: Director of Operations
text:
The short version

Cenfire makes a new kind of switch: an all-silicon MEMS switch, built on a CMOS-compatible silicon spring instead of the metal springs of the past. Our first product, CF2140, is a signal and measurement switch for semiconductor test. It is finishing qualification now, and our second product starts qualification right behind it.

Making a product that works is one thing. Making it on schedule and at cost, month after month, through outside fabs, packaging and test houses, is another. We need the person who builds that machine. You will write the production ramp plan, get it approved, and then own it: wafer starts, packaging, test, inventory, second sources, distribution and customer shipment, for more than one product at a time.

What you will do

**Own the ramp plan.**
 In your first 90 days, map the CF2140 flow from wafer starts to shipment, set baselines for yield, cycle time and on-time delivery, and write the production ramp plan for CEO approval. After that, the plan and its results are yours.

**Run the weekly build plan.**
 Coordinate fab, packaging, test and shipments across every product in qualification or production. Assign owners and recovery dates when lots slip or material runs short. Commit to customers only what the plan can support.

**Run overlapping ramps.**
 Plan the second product's qualification builds alongside the first product's production ramp. Share wafers, test capacity and people between them deliberately, not by accident.

**Build the supply chain.**
 Manage our fab, packaging and test partners. Find and qualify second sources for the steps that carry the most risk. Set up the distribution channel that will serve our smaller customers.

**Build the operating system.**
 Lot traceability, ERP and MRP transactions, inventory accuracy and shipment reporting that people can trust.

**Lead through others, then build a team.**
 You start with no direct reports. You will work through Cenfire's engineering, quality and test staff, setting clear owners and deadlines. As volume grows, you will build the operations team, and some existing staff may move under you.

What you bring

**Required**

* You have personally taken a semiconductor, MEMS or comparable hardware product from qualification or pilot builds into repeatable production.
* You have planned across external wafer fabrication, packaging and test: yield loss, minimum lot sizes, lead times and constrained capacity.
* You have owned procurement, inventory, production scheduling, logistics and supplier performance, and you have implemented or improved ERP or MRP workflows.
* You make build and sourcing decisions from yield by stage and cost per good unit.
* You can lead people who don't report to you, and you can explain trade-offs plainly to engineering, quality, sales and the CEO.
* A degree in engineering, manufacturing or supply chain, or equivalent practical experience.

**Strongly preferred**

* You have run more than one product through overlapping qualification and production ramps.
* You have qualified second sources for fab, packaging or test.
* You have set up or worked with distributors.
* You have done this at a small company, with limited staff and systems.

Why you would want this

* **You build the operations function**
  behind a new switching platform, with direct ownership of production scale and customer delivery.
* **You own the plan.**
  You write the ramp plan. You don't inherit someone else's.
* **The path is defined.**
  The next step is Vice President of Operations: owning the operations budget, capacity and sourcing strategy, and the operations organization across product lines.
* **You work directly with the CEO**
  and a small founding team.

Logistics

* Full-time onsite in Goleta, California, with travel to suppliers as needed.
* Reports to Seena Partokia, CEO.
* Stock options with 4-year vesting and a 1-year cliff.
* Base salary $160,000 to $180,000.
* We do not sponsor work visas or provide relocation assistance.
